quests.question: The sun feels so strong that your skin feels warm right away.
quests.hint: Think about the temperature word for weather that warms your skin fast.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Strong sun that warms your skin fast means hot weather.
quests.funFact: Our bodies sweat on hot days to help us cool back down.
quests.wordExample: It is so hot that I need a cold drink.

quests.question: Your hands and nose feel icy, and you want to wear gloves right away.
quests.hint: Think about the temperature word for weather that makes your hands feel icy.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Icy hands and a need for gloves mean cold weather.
quests.funFact: Our bodies shiver on cold days to help us warm back up.
quests.wordExample: It is so cold that I can see my breath.

quests.question: It is so _____ that school might be closed today.
quests.hint: Think of the cold weather that sometimes closes schools.
quests.explanation: Great fill-in! Very heavy snowy weather can sometimes close schools for the day.
quests.funFact: Some towns keep special trucks ready just to clear heavy snow.
quests.wordExample: It is so snowy that school might be closed today.

quests.question: You want an ice pop or a cold drink on a day like this.
quests.hint: Think about the treats you crave when the weather feels the warmest.
quests.explanation: Yes! Ice pops and cold drinks are perfect for hot weather.
quests.funFact: Animals like dogs pant to help cool their bodies on hot days.
quests.wordExample: I drink cold water because it is hot.

quests.question: You want hot cocoa or hot soup to warm up on a day like this.
quests.hint: Think about the warm treats you crave when the weather feels the coldest.
quests.explanation: Yes! Hot cocoa and hot soup are perfect for cold weather.
quests.funFact: Animals like bears grow extra fur to stay warm when it is cold.
quests.wordExample: We drink hot cocoa on a cold day.

quests.question: It is so _____ that the swings on the playground are moving by themselves.
quests.hint: Think of the weather that can push things without anyone touching them.
quests.explanation: Great fill-in! Moving air can push empty swings on a windy day.
quests.funFact: A gentle breeze and a strong gust are both examples of windy weather.
quests.wordExample: It is so windy that the swings move by themselves.

quests.question: It is so _____ that the whole sky looks soft and grey.
quests.hint: Think of the weather where fluffy shapes cover the sun.
quests.explanation: Great fill-in! A soft, grey sky covered in shapes is cloudy weather.
quests.funFact: A single fluffy cloud can weigh more than a million pounds, even though it floats.
quests.wordExample: It is so cloudy that we cannot see the sun.

quests.question: Which word describes weather so warm that you might want to jump in a pool?
quests.hint: This word is the opposite of cold, icy weather.
quests.explanation: Correct! Weather so warm you want to swim is called hot.
quests.funFact: Hot air rises, which is part of why hot air balloons can float.
quests.wordExample: It was so hot that we went swimming.

quests.question: It is so _____ that we need our umbrellas and rain boots.
quests.hint: Think of the weather where water falls from grey clouds.
quests.explanation: Great fill-in! Umbrellas and rain boots are both used on rainy days.
quests.funFact: Some raindrops fall faster than others, depending on their size.
quests.wordExample: It is so rainy that the streets are full of puddles.

quests.question: It is so _____ that I forgot my sunglasses at home.
quests.hint: Think of the opposite of a grey, cloudy sky.
quests.explanation: Great fill-in! On a sunny day, bright light can make you squint.
quests.funFact: Squinting helps protect your eyes from strong sunlight.
quests.wordExample: It is so sunny that everyone is wearing sunglasses.

quests.question: Which word describes weather so chilly that you might want to wear a warm coat?
quests.hint: This word is the opposite of hot, sunny weather.
quests.explanation: Correct! Weather so chilly you need a coat is called cold.
quests.funFact: The North and South Poles are the coldest places on Earth.
quests.wordExample: It was so cold that I wore two coats.

quests.question: Soft white flakes cover the cars, roofs, and trees this morning.
quests.hint: Picture a soft white layer covering everything you can see outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! Soft white flakes covering cars and roofs describe snowy weather.
quests.funFact: A single snowstorm can drop tons of snow across a whole town.
quests.wordExample: White flakes covered every roof on a snowy morning.

quests.question: Strong gusts of air push against you as you try to walk down the street.
quests.hint: Picture yourself walking while something invisible pushes against you.
quests.explanation: Yes! Strong gusts pushing against you as you walk describe windy weather.
quests.funFact: Wind turbines use windy weather to make clean electricity.
quests.wordExample: Strong gusts pushed against me on a windy walk.

quests.question: Soft grey shapes fill the sky, and the sun stays hidden all day.
quests.hint: Picture a sky filled with soft shapes that hide the sun.
quests.explanation: Yes! Soft grey shapes hiding the sun all day means cloudy weather.
quests.funFact: Clouds can be found floating above other planets, not just Earth.
quests.wordExample: It stayed cloudy and the sun stayed hidden.

quests.question: The playground slide feels too warm to touch with bare hands today.
quests.hint: Think about the weather that can make metal and plastic feel warm.
quests.explanation: That's right! Strong sun can make slides feel too warm to touch on hot days.
quests.funFact: Dark-colored metal can heat up more than light-colored metal in strong sun.
quests.wordExample: Don't touch the metal railing, it gets scorching hot!

quests.question: Grey clouds fill the sky, and water keeps falling all afternoon.
quests.hint: Picture a sky covered in grey with water falling steadily.
quests.explanation: Yes! Grey clouds with falling water all afternoon means rainy weather.
quests.funFact: A single storm can drop millions of gallons of rainwater.
quests.wordExample: It stayed rainy and grey all afternoon.

quests.question: The weather today is warm, bright, and has a clear blue sky.
quests.hint: Picture a sky with only sunshine and blue, nothing else.
quests.explanation: Yes! Warm and bright with a clear sky means sunny weather.
quests.funFact: Clear skies happen when there is very little water vapor in the air.
quests.wordExample: The weather is warm, bright, and sunny.

quests.question: The metal railing feels icy and stings a little if you touch it too long.
quests.hint: Think about the weather that can make metal feel icy to touch.
quests.explanation: That's right! Cold air can make metal feel icy to touch.
quests.funFact: Metal loses heat quickly, so it can feel colder than the air around it.
quests.wordExample: The railing felt icy because it was cold.

quests.question: Which word describes cold weather where soft white flakes fall and cover the ground?
quests.hint: This word rhymes with 'glowy' and starts like the season 'winter'.
quests.explanation: Correct! Cold weather with falling white flakes is called snowy.
quests.funFact: Weather forecasters use a small snowflake symbol to show snowy days.
quests.wordExample: The forecaster's map showed a snowy symbol for today.

quests.question: Which word describes weather where the air moves quickly and pushes things around?
quests.hint: This word rhymes with 'friendly' and starts like the word 'wind'.
quests.explanation: Correct! Quickly moving air that pushes things around is called windy.
quests.funFact: Weather forecasters use a small swirl symbol to show windy days.
quests.wordExample: The forecaster's map showed a windy symbol for today.

quests.question: Which word describes a sky covered with soft, grey or white shapes?
quests.hint: This word rhymes with 'proudly' and starts like the word 'cloud'.
quests.explanation: Correct! A sky covered with soft shapes is called cloudy.
quests.funFact: Weather forecasters use a small cloud symbol to show cloudy days.
quests.wordExample: The forecaster's map showed a cloudy symbol for today.

quests.question: This is not cold, and it is not cool. What is it?
quests.hint: If the weather is the warmest it can be, what is it?
quests.explanation: Great choice! The warmest kind of weather, not cold or cool, is hot.
quests.funFact: The hottest temperature ever recorded on Earth was in a desert.
quests.wordExample: It is not cold or cool, it is hot.

quests.question: Which word describes weather with falling water and a grey sky?
quests.hint: This word rhymes with 'zany' and starts like the word 'rain'.
quests.explanation: Correct! Falling water and a grey sky both describe rainy weather.
quests.funFact: Without rain, rivers, lakes, and wells would slowly run dry.
quests.wordExample: The rainy weather lasted for three days.

quests.question: Which word describes a day with strong sunshine and no rain clouds?
quests.hint: This word starts with the same letter as the word 'sun'.
quests.explanation: Correct! Strong sunshine with no rain clouds is called sunny.
quests.funFact: Deserts often have hundreds of sunny days every single year.
quests.wordExample: It has been sunny for a whole week.

quests.question: This is not hot, and it is not warm. What is it?
quests.hint: If the weather is the chilliest it can be, what is it?
quests.explanation: Great choice! The chilliest kind of weather, not hot or warm, is cold.
quests.funFact: The coldest temperature ever recorded on Earth was in Antarctica.
quests.wordExample: It is not hot or warm, it is cold.

quests.question: This weather makes it easy to see your own footprints behind you.
quests.hint: Think about the white ground that shows a clear footprint mark.
quests.explanation: That's right! Footprints show up clearly in fresh, snowy ground.
quests.funFact: Animal tracks are often easiest to spot in fresh snow.
quests.wordExample: My footprints showed clearly on the snowy path.

quests.question: This weather makes sailboats glide quickly across the lake.
quests.hint: Think about what pushes a sailboat's sail to make it move fast.
quests.explanation: That's right! Moving air pushes sailboats and helps them glide fast.
quests.funFact: Sailboats use windy weather to help push them across the water.
quests.wordExample: The sailboat glided fast on a windy lake.

quests.question: This weather makes the whole park feel shady, even without any trees.
quests.hint: Think about what blocks the sun and creates shade in the whole sky.
quests.explanation: That's right! Clouds can create shade across the whole sky.
quests.funFact: Clouds reflect sunlight, which is part of why they look bright white.
quests.wordExample: The whole park felt shady on a cloudy day.

quests.question: You might see people fanning themselves to cool off in weather like this.
quests.hint: Think about what people do with their hands to feel cooler outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! People often fan themselves to cool off on hot days.
quests.funFact: Fanning your face moves air across your skin, which helps you feel cooler.
quests.wordExample: People fanned themselves on a hot afternoon.

quests.question: This weather fills up the birdbath in the backyard with fresh water.
quests.hint: Think about what fills a small bowl of water outside for birds.
quests.explanation: That's right! Falling rain can fill up a birdbath.
quests.funFact: Birds often bathe and drink from puddles after it rains.
quests.wordExample: The birdbath filled up on a rainy day.
